question: In the pyrolysis of oil shale kerogen, by how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss
rendered:
According to the document, under air, the characteristic H2 signal appears at lower temperatures (approximately 250−600 °C, with a maximum near 330 °C), whereas under nitrogen, the H2 signal appears at higher temperatures (approximately 300−800 °C, with a maximum near 450 °C). 

Therefore, the maximum of the H2 signal occurs approximately 120 °C earlier under air than under nitrogen (450 °C - 330 °C = 120 °C).
